questions.stem: Let p = "T1 commits" and q = "T2 commits". Which formula says "T2 commits only if T1 commits"?
questions.explain: "q only if p" means q cannot happen without p, which is q → p. The reverse p → q says something different.

questions.stem: Which statement is the negation of "every transaction committed"?
questions.explain: To deny "all", one counter-example is enough: at least one transaction did not commit.

questions.stem: T1 touches the items {A, B} and T2 touches {B, C, D}. How many items do both transactions touch?
questions.explain: The shared items are the intersection {B}, which has 1 element.

questions.stem: The table accounts has one row, (id = 1, bal = 500). After `UPDATE accounts SET bal = bal - 100 WHERE id = 1`, what is bal?
questions.explain: The update subtracts 100 from the old balance: 500 − 100 = 400.

questions.stem: The table accounts has balances 500, 300 and 200. What does `SELECT SUM(bal) FROM accounts` return?
